batch_entity.name: git-serious double-tap: tap machinery projection v0.6.0

batch_node.name: git-serious double-tap: tap machinery projection v0.6.0
batch_node.description: The tap-specific machinery picture (req-git-serious-double-tap-tap-projection): a double-tap-owned projection whose one elevation runs TWO layouts on the same canvas — git_serious's machinery layout (github_core's machinery.js, referenced by entity id, never copied) and then the tap lanes layout (this plugin's tap-machinery.js), which regroups the repository's workflows into lanes by what starts them (PR gate · publish · scheduled · fleet · reusable baseline), places them by the cardinal map ruled 2026-09-09 (gate centre, publish left, scheduled below, fleet and baseline at the bottom, sources right), and draws the workflow-call and workflow_run edges across lanes. One graph panel owns the projection and shares the generic repository page's three scene searches by id; the tap page mounts it with the fixed input repo=unified-systems-com/tap. Out-of-file endpoints: git_serious's layout and searches, so git_serious seeds first. v0.2.0 (git-serious-double-tap#34): zizmor's verdict on every workflow card as three more status-badge sets owned by this projection — actionable findings (High/Medium, purple), advisory findings (Low/Informational, light purple), and NOT SCANNED (grey, the vocabulary already meaning we could not say) — each fed by a projection-mode search in this bundle; unparameterized on purpose, because badge searches take static inputs and the badge renders only on hosts present in the scene. Projection node upsert plus six search nodes; every prior id stable, batch id moved. v0.3.0 (tap#426): every finding row in a zizmor badge's info window links to the finding on /zizmor/finding — the detail searches return the finding's own id as finding_id and the three zizmor badge sets declare row_url_template over it. Search + projection node upserts; every id stable, batch id moved. v0.4.0 (George, 2026-09-10): the advisory (Low/Informational) badge is gone — one purple badge, actionable findings only; the table beneath still lists every severity. Its two searches leave the bundle; on a grid that already holds them they stay as unreferenced search nodes until an operator deletes them (a shipped bundle cannot express 'gone'). v0.5.0 (git-serious-double-tap#31): workflow and job clicks open github_core's workflow page by workflow_id, the key it takes since tap-plugin-github-core#101. Panel node upsert only. v0.6.0 (George, 2026-09-10): lock_nodes — the picture is a placed layout, not a sandbox; nothing drags once drawn (badges still open their info windows). Projection node upsert only.

node.name: double-tap tap lanes layout
node.description: Runs after machinery.js on the same cy: classifies each workflow by its primary trigger (pull_request/merge_group > push > workflow_run > schedule > workflow_call > dispatch), promotes a workflow_call workflow to the reusable baseline when callers span more than one lane, groups the workflow boxes under synthetic lane parents inside the repository box, lays the lanes out by the cardinal map, re-seats sources and outputs around the new block, and adds synthetic call/workflow_run edges. Reads nothing that names tap; the lanes are derived from collected workflow configuration.

node.name: Machinery · tap lanes
node.description: unified-systems-com/tap's CI system as lanes: the PR gate front and centre, the publish chain to its left ending in the outputs, scheduled lanes below, the fleet lanes and the reusable baseline at the bottom, sources on the right. github_core's machinery projection drawn first, the tap lanes layout over it (the double-tap's own projection). Shares the generic repository page's scene searches; the page pins repo=unified-systems-com/tap. GitHub nodes open their html_url in a new tab; a workflow box opens that workflow's page (github_core's generic workflow-and-job viewer) instead — the anatomy and its runs, with the link out to GitHub on the identity row.

entity.name: double-tap — actionable zizmor findings per workflow (count)

node.name: double-tap — actionable zizmor findings per workflow (count)
node.description: How many High or Medium zizmor findings sit on each workflow's file. Cumulative, not current: zizmor does not tombstone yet (zizmor-tap#27), so a finding fixed since it was first seen still counts. Badge population rows (entity_id + count) per spec-viz-status-badge-info; org-wide on purpose — the badge renders only on workflow cards present in the scene.

query: RETURN w.entity_id AS entity_id, COUNT(f.entity_id) AS count

entity.name: double-tap — actionable zizmor findings per workflow (detail)

node.name: double-tap — actionable zizmor findings per workflow (detail)
node.description: Info-window rows for the actionable badge: one per High or Medium finding, named by zizmor's summary; audit, severity and job ride along for a later columns config. finding_id is the finding's own entity id, the placeholder the badge set's row_url_template fills (tap#426).

query: RETURN w.entity_id AS entity_id, f.data.summary AS name, f.data.audit_id AS audit, f.data.severity AS severity, f.data.location.job_key AS job, f.entity_id AS finding_id

entity.name: double-tap — workflows zizmor could not scan (count)

node.name: double-tap — workflows zizmor could not scan (count)
node.description: The third state on the graph: workflows whose SCANNED_WORKFLOW outcome is anything but `evaluated` (no-yaml, parse-failed). A card with neither a purple nor a grey badge means zizmor READ the file and found nothing; this grey badge means it could not read it, so its findings are UNKNOWN, not zero. Edge properties are addressed as e.data.properties.<key>.

query: RETURN w.entity_id AS entity_id, COUNT(w.entity_id) AS count

node.name: double-tap — workflows zizmor could not scan (detail)
